edges.effect_quant: Systematic review evidence supports chlorhexidine mouthwash as an adjunct for reducing plaque and gingivitis, with one evidence summary reporting about 33% plaque reduction and 26% gingivitis reduction versus control conditions. Controlled trials also show consistent short-term improvements in gingival and plaque indices versus placebo.
edges.population: children and adults using chlorhexidine mouthwash as an adjunct to routine oral hygiene
edges.mechanism: Chlorhexidine has broad antimicrobial action and substantive binding in the oral cavity, which suppresses plaque biofilm accumulation and lowers inflammatory gingival response during short-term use.
edges.summary: This is a reasonably well-supported adjunctive oral-hygiene edge. Chlorhexidine mouthwash reliably lowers gingivitis and plaque scores in short-term trials and systematic reviews, although it is best viewed as a targeted adjunct rather than a routine indefinite therapy.
edges.caveats: The main benefit is short-term gingival control, while long-term use is limited by staining, taste disturbance, and calculus buildup. Much of the literature focuses on surrogate plaque and gingival indices rather than hard long-run periodontal outcomes.
